events.text: A message comes from {b3_agent} sleeping inside {b3_foe}, where they pass as a gate-boy at their training hall and work in the porch where visitors take off their boots. It is folded small and passed along by a pedlar who thinks it is a love letter. This time it carries which families send their children there, and which have stopped. At the bottom, in another hand, they have added: I am well.

choices.text: Act on it quietly

effects.log: You act on it quietly, through a cousin and a carter, so nobody guesses the source. The advantage is real, and it costs you a night of sleep.

choices.text: Hold it for the right season

effects.log: You hold it for the right season. News is like cheese; some keeps, and some turns, and you are never sure which you have.

choices.text: Write back, and ask after their health

effects.log: You write back, and ask after their health and their spirits before anything else. It is a small thing that matters more than the news.

events.text: Word comes, late and in a hurry, that {b3_agent} in {b3_foe} very nearly gave themselves away: a porter who knows every cough in the district remarked on a way of bowing too neatly in front of three students. They talked their way out of it. They say so cheerfully, and the cheerfulness is how you know how frightened they were.

choices.text: Tell them to come home

effects.log: You tell them to come home, and they refuse, with polite stubbornness. You do not press. They have earned the right to be wrong.

choices.text: Send a warning and a cure

effects.log: You send a coded warning, and a trick for hiding exactly that fault. The next letter comes with a joke in it, and you feel better.

choices.text: Tell them to keep going

effects.log: You tell them to keep going, as the school requires. It is easy to write. It is the sort of letter you reread at night and wish you had not sent.

events.text: On the first dawn after the binding, at the gate of the yard, the youngest pupil stops short at the sight of the great, still shape settled across the threshold. The beast, {b3_beast}, does not look up. It has a slow, steady calm that hushes the shutters. You have the odd, vain feeling of being measured by something that has measured a great many people before you and found most of them wanting.

choices.text: Greet it by name, formally

effects.log: You greet it by the name you gave it, with the bow due an elder. It tilts its head, once. The yard exhales, and the matter is settled.

choices.text: Share your breakfast

effects.log: You share your breakfast, which it accepts with ceremony. Everyone who sees this tells the story, and each makes the portion larger.

choices.text: Leave it be, and keep watch

effects.log: You leave it be, and keep watch from a distance, as one does with a sleeping elder. It is respectful, and slightly absurd.

events.text: A trapper with a very fine net and a very poor reputation has been seen on the paths above the gate of the yard. The youngest pupil says the beast, {b3_beast}, was restless last night, circling, as if aware. The trapper's price has been rising among those who deal in such things, and the trapper has a cart.

choices.text: Drive him off yourself

ok.log: You drive the trapper off the hill, firmly, and the beast watches from the arch with an expression of mild approval. It stays closer to you after.

fail.log: The trapper slips past you, and it takes your beast a whole night to chase him off. You are embarrassed in the morning, and the beast is gentle about it.

choices.text: Set a watch on the gate

effects.log: You set a watch on the gate, three pupils to a night, and a bell. The trapper tries it once, and the beast watches him fail.

choices.text: Send him after easier prey

effects.log: You let it be known that a fatter, stupider quarry roams the far hills. It is not nice. It works.

events.text: The beast of your line, {b3_beast}, settles across the threshold every dusk, and everyone has made their peace with it. It also shreds the doormats, and no one has made their peace with that. Today the gate is full of grumbling neighbours, a dozen complaints, and a beast looking blandly at the sky.

choices.text: Fine the beast an extra helping

effects.log: You fine the beast an extra bone, and it accepts the punishment with resignation. The neighbours leave satisfied, and the beast leaves content.

choices.text: Explain that it is old

effects.log: You explain that it is very old, and was here before the neighbours. They concede, because it is true, and because it is looking at them.

choices.text: Coax it somewhere quieter

effects.log: You coax it somewhere quieter with a bowl of something warm. It sulks for a month, then settles.

events.text: Something wild stirs in the beast, {b3_beast}, one spring: it stands at the gate all night, looking at the far hills and making a low, unfamiliar sound. The pupils keep their distance. It is clearly homesick, or called, and it does not belong to you, in the end.

choices.text: Open the gate for a season

effects.log: You open the gate and let it go for a season. It returns after a hundred days, gaunt and content, and settles as if it had never left.

choices.text: Keep the gate shut, and stay near

effects.log: You keep the gate shut, and stay near, talking until the mood passes. It does, eventually, but something has shifted between you.

choices.text: Walk out with it into the night

effects.log: You walk out with it into the night, the two of you, as far as the edge of the fields. It stops. It looks at you. It turns back.
